paragraphs: Apple’s long-awaited entry into the smart home is finally about to become a reality. The company is reportedly preparing to launch its first dedicated smart home hub on October 13.
The device could give Apple its first real answer to products such as Amazon’s Echo Show and Google’s Nest Hub, according to an unconfirmed report published Wednesday.

Apple reportedly will unveil the new product alongside two other smart home devices: updated versions of the HomePod mini and Apple TV set-top box. All will be designed around the new AI-powered Siri digital assistant.
Apple already offers HomeKit and the Home app, but its smart home hardware lineup has largely been limited to the HomePod and Apple TV.
That’s apparently about to change with the much-rumored smart home hub, as well as new versions of the smart speaker and streaming box, reports Bloomberg.

The centerpiece of Apple’s latest move into the smart home market will reportedly pack a roughly 6-inch square display. Apple is expected to offer one version that sits on a countertop and one that can be mounted on a wall.

The countertop model reportedly uses a design reminiscent of the iMac G4 — aka the “sunflower Mac.” A metal arm connects the display to a rounded base containing speakers and microphones, while allowing the screen to tilt. The wall-mounted version has a thinner base.

The hub is supposedly about as thick as an iPhone with bezels similar to older iPads. But this is not a mobile product. There’s no built-in battery, and the smart home hub must remain connected to power through USB-C.
